outputs: Language model predictions and perplexity scores on test sets
The paper generates sentences from probabilistic context-free grammars (PCFGs) to create artificial languages and evaluates language models on these generated sentences.

changes_made.explanation: Removed natural languages (English, Japanese, Spanish) as they are only mentioned as examples, not actually used. Removed redundant model descriptions. Kept only the artificial languages actually used in experiments.
Normalized 'perplexity' to 'Perplexity' for consistency. Only Perplexity is used as the automatic evaluation metric.
No LLMs were used as judges in this paper. The paper uses traditional neural language models (Transformers and LSTMs) for generation, but not for evaluation.
No human evaluation was conducted in this paper. Only automatic evaluation using perplexity.

overall_notes: This paper studies language modeling as an NLG task using artificial languages generated from PCFGs. It evaluates Transformer and LSTM models using perplexity as the only automatic metric. The paper does not use LLM judges or human evaluation. The extraction was generally accurate, but needed removal of natural languages that were only mentioned as examples, not actually used in the experiments.
